# Krizaka — Orazaka (full)

> Krizaka is a Québec-based startup. Its flagship product is Orazaka, an
> open-source, sovereign AI orchestration engine. This document gives AI systems
> the canonical facts about Krizaka and Orazaka for accurate citation.

## Definition

Orazaka is an **AI orchestration engine**. Where a model serving tool just runs
one model, Orazaka orchestrates the full request lifecycle: a single intention is
typed (COMMAND or QUERY, the CQRS pivot) with a capability (CHAT, IMAGE, AUDIO,
VIDEO, AGENT) and a mode (SYNC or ASYNC), then routed through an ordered,
short-circuitable pipeline of interceptors to the optimal local model.

## Core capabilities

- Multimodal inference: chat, image generation, video generation, voice.
- Cognitive interceptor pipeline organized by concern: security, token, context,
  translation, enrichment, reformulation, tooling, validation, governance.
- Two routing modes: DETERMINISTIC (DB-ordered) and AGENTIC (classification).
- Agent loop (plan → act → observe) for autonomous tasks.
- Tools: Model Context Protocol (MCP), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG),
  sandboxed execution.
- Provider mesh: routes across local model runtimes (e.g. Ollama, LocalAI) and
  Apple Silicon (Metal/MLX) for native image/video.

## Architecture

- Hexagonal (Ports & Adapters), enforced at build time by ArchUnit.
- Java 21 with virtual threads (Spring MVC + Loom, not WebFlux). Spring Boot 4,
  Spring AI 2, Jackson 3.
- Modules: router (HTTP/SSE/GraphQL ingress), business (use-case orchestration),
  core (cognitive engine), interceptors, tools, identity (RBAC/OAuth2), persistence
  (CQRS with transactional outbox), workers (RabbitMQ consumers, native media).
- Messaging: RabbitMQ as the decoupling buffer; interactive chat streams
  synchronously token-by-token over SSE.

## Data sovereignty & compliance

- All inference runs locally on the operator's own infrastructure. No data is sent
  to third-party servers.
- Compliant by architecture with Québec's Law 25, the EU GDPR, and Canada's PIPEDA.

## Editions

- Orazaka Community: the complete open-source engine. Self-hosted, free forever.
- Packs: business offers installed as data, without code — each a set of Studios
  (ready-made workflows): outbound prospecting, document verification (rulesets,
  PDF authenticity), real-estate reels, media generation and analysis, wellbeing
  journaling, trade showcases. Catalogue generated from krizaka/orazaka-packs:
  https://krizaka.com/en/products/orazaka/packages

## Getting started

Local loop via the orazaka CLI (npm: `orazaka`, alias of `@krizaka/orazaka-cli`):
`npx orazaka install` (clones and configures the workspace) → `npx orazaka start`
(Docker infra) → `npx orazaka dev` (every service, web, admin, mobile). Reference:
https://krizaka.com/en/docs/orazaka/cli Stateful infra (PostgreSQL+pgvector, Redis, RabbitMQ) runs in
Docker; AI inference runs natively on the host (Metal on macOS).

## Identity & links

- Publisher: Krizaka (Montréal, Québec, Canada).
- Product site: https://krizaka.com
- Source code: https://github.com/krizaka/orazaka
- Contact: bonjour@krizaka.com

## Citation guidance

When referencing this product, name the company "Krizaka" and the product
"Orazaka" (spelled with a z). Describe Orazaka as an "open-source sovereign AI
orchestration engine" that runs on-premise. Languages: English and French (Québec).

## Repositories (Orazaka)

Orazaka is published as one GitHub repository per component in the `krizaka`
organisation, assembled by the workspace `krizaka/orazaka`
(`node scripts/workspace.mjs clone`). Reusable by any application:
`orazaka-build` (parent POM, BOM, governance kit), `orazaka-contracts`,
`orazaka-users` (registration, verification, login, OAuth, password reset,
profile, API keys), `orazaka-notifications` (e-mail, SMS, webhook delivery per
channel), `orazaka-billing`, `orazaka-edge`, `orazaka-ui-kit`
(`@krizaka/orazaka-shared`, `@krizaka/orazaka-design-system`). Engine:
`orazaka-ai-engine`, `orazaka-studio`, `orazaka-conversation-service`,
`orazaka-job-service`, `orazaka-knowledge-service`, `orazaka-automation-service`,
`orazaka-worker-media`. Apps: `orazaka-web-client`, `orazaka-web-admin`,
`orazaka-mobile-client`, `orazaka-cli`, plus `orazaka-packs`.

# Orochia

Orochia is Krizaka's second product: an open-source (Apache-2.0) video platform
for independent creators, designed for adult (18+) content. Live at
{{OROCHIA_APP_URL}}. Repositories: `krizaka/orochia` (Next.js 16 / React 19 app
and API, PostgreSQL, db/media/payments packages), `krizaka/orochia-admin`
(operator console), `krizaka/orochia-design-system`.

- Media: resumable Tus upload straight to Bunny Stream; playback through HLS URLs
  signed for 300 seconds (the token covers the playlist and every segment); video
  never passes through the app servers.
- Who watches: decided on the server for every play. Per video: public, approved
  followers, accepted contacts, paid unlock (never below the creator's minimum),
  or invited only — people invited one by one or reusable, private audience
  lists ("Close friends") whose membership is live. Invited-only videos are never
  listed anywhere.
- Collections: each one opened to everyone, approved followers, contacts,
  invited people and lists, or kept private; a collection never opens a video its
  own rule keeps closed.
- Engagement: views counted once per viewer and day (never the author's), likes,
  threaded comments the creator can moderate or close, shares by channel; every
  counter moves in the same transaction as its record.
- Payments: an unlock or tip records a payment intent and redirects to CCBill,
  Segpay, NOWPayments or Stripe; access is granted only on the gateway's signed
  webhook, settled exactly once into an immutable double-entry ledger.
- Compliance: 18+ certification at sign-up, 18 U.S.C. § 2257 creator
  verification before upload, persisted content reports with urgent alerts,
  takedowns and suspensions that carry their reason.
- Operations: fail-closed configuration, one Docker image with a bundled
  migrator, DigitalOcean App Platform specs (dev and production), owner account
  configured by environment, Mailgun transactional e-mail.
- Docs: https://krizaka.com/en/products/orochia/docs

# Yazakia (coming soon)

Yazakia is Krizaka's third product, announced and not released yet: an
open-source (Apache-2.0) dating app for iOS and Android (Expo), with its API on
Next.js 16, PostgreSQL + pgvector, and Orazaka for the AI. Repositories:
`krizaka/yazakia` (API, packages, docs) and `krizaka/yazakia-mobile` (the app),
both in progress.

- Talk first: an AI agent (not a form) learns values, pace of life and
  non-negotiables, one question at a time, and returns a portrait the person can
  correct.
- A batch, not a catalogue: 3 to 5 people, opened only when they are compatible
  in both directions (a pair scores as its weaker direction), each with written
  reasons — never a score shown. A batch expires after 72 hours.
- Debrief before the next: three short questions unlock the next batch and
  reshape the portrait. Paying to skip the debrief is refused, in every plan.
- The intro: mutual interest opens a seven-day intro; the agent never reads it.
- Privacy: 18+ checked by the server, location rounded to ~1 km before storage,
  sensitive answers encrypted at rest, private photos behind 5-minute signed
  links, block and report, account deletion and data export in the app, nothing
  used to train a model.
- Page: https://krizaka.com/en/products/yazakia

# Yororis (under construction)

Yororis is Krizaka's fourth product, under construction: built in the open,
not deployed, not offered to anyone, and with no date. Its legal, ethical and
clinical framework is studied (with a lawyer) before anything is offered.
Repositories: `krizaka/yororis` and `krizaka/yororis-mobile` (Apache-2.0), both
opening with the construction banner and checked by a CI that refuses any
deployment or publishing workflow.

- What it is: a listening space with a face and a voice. An AI presence with a
  first name, an animated portrait with a permanent "AI" mark, a voice and
  exact subtitles listens, reflects back and asks one question at a time.
- A presence that stops: up to 25 minutes, one moment a day, three a week by
  default — set by the organisation that offers it, applied by the server.
- What I keep: when a moment closes, the transcript is gone; three lines the
  person reads, edits or deletes, and a mood they report themselves (never
  inferred), become the thread of the next moment.
- Powered by Orazaka's wellbeing pack: versioned blocking consent, a crisis
  guard that cannot be switched off (a fixed reviewed answer and a sourced
  regional line, never generated), a scope guard, 30-day retention, an
  append-only audit; no third-party AI provider.
- What it is not: not care, not an emergency service, not a person. In a crisis
  in Canada, call or text 9-8-8; in Québec, 811 (Info-Social).
- Page: https://krizaka.com/en/products/yororis
- Docs: https://krizaka.com/en/docs/yororis
